round: 2026-10-02 review (the mega review of the preview site)
note: October 2, 2026: the owner went through every toy on the preview site and named the sounds to change; every toy he called perfect or fine stays as it is. Two notes cover every toy: when a tap pauses an effect, its sound must pause and resume with it; and a toy's first tap often sounds late (later taps are in sync). He still wants subtle, realistic sounds, often real recordings, with no wind unless it belongs, no motor 'vroom', no buzz or horn and no robotic tones. The full review is docs/reviews/2026-10-02-mega-review/review.md.

raspberry.note: It sounds too much like bubbles.
raspberry.plan: A real juicy squish as the drupelets break off, then a soft tap for each one landing on the table, and a small squish as they come back (no bubbles).

blackberry.note: Like the raspberry, it sounds too much like bubbles.
blackberry.plan: A darker, deeper real squish, the drupelets tapping down on the table as they bounce, and a soft squish as they spring back (no bubbles).

star-cookie.note: It sounds like a zipper, not a cookie breaking apart.
star-cookie.plan: A real crisp snap and crumble as it breaks, and a small soft crumble as it puts itself back together.

mandeltorus.note: It sounds too robotic; he'd like something similar to the Mandelbulb's sound, which he loves.
mandeltorus.plan: Like the Mandelbulb: a low drone with a ratchet as the rings start to turn, and again as they lock back.

garden-gnome.note: A little weird; he doesn't like the chirp at the start.
garden-gnome.plan: A soft stone thud as the gnome lands from its hop, and a match-like flare and soft flame as its lantern lights (no chirp, no click).

lantern.note: He doesn't like the click; he wants something more suitable.
lantern.plan: A real match strike and a soft flame catching when it lights; a real puff blowing it out.

wooden-elephant.note: It should trumpet like a real elephant.
wooden-elephant.plan: A light wooden knock, then a real elephant trumpeting as the trunk lifts.

alarm-clock.note: It sounds like a wooden instrument, not an alarm clock; it should sound like a real one.
alarm-clock.plan: A real mechanical twin-bell alarm ringing while the clock rattles (2.3 s).

vintage-camera.note: The flash is too clicky; it should sound realistic.
vintage-camera.plan: A real vintage press camera: a soft shutter and the whoomph of the flash powder.

carrot-cake.note: Acceptable but underwhelming and very simple; a better one would be welcome, otherwise leave it.
carrot-cake.plan: A softer knife slide, a moist crumb as the slice lifts out, and the same soft plate thud.

cat-statue.note: It should meow like a real cat.
cat-statue.plan: A soft stone scrape as the head turns, then a real cat's meow as it tilts.

horse-statue.note: The whinny sounds like a whistle; it should be a real horse whinny or neigh.
horse-statue.plan: A soft stone scrape, a real horse's whinny as it rears, and a stone thud as it lands.

tin-can-real.note: Drop the drum hit and the coin-like ring; just a plain metallic roll.
tin-can-real.plan: Now: One real recording of an empty can rolling on a hard floor, slowing and settling; no drum hit, no coin ring (Sound C).

donut.note: Sounds too wet; find a better one (right direction).
donut.plan: Now: A soft, dry tear as it pulls apart (a real bread tear) and a soft pat as the halves meet; nothing wet (Sound C).

knot.note: The jelly sounds dirty; pick something else (the other knots' sound is fine).
knot.plan: Now: the torus knot's sound, timed to this knot: it strains as the loops tie tighter, then lets go with a soft thump and swish as it relaxes; no jelly (Sound D).

planet.note: Too much wind: loud enough to hurt the ears (the wind is too strong on many toys).
planet.plan: A quiet, darker breeze and a soft low whoosh as the clouds race round.

tennis-ball.note: It sounds like a ping-pong ball; it should sound like a real tennis ball.
tennis-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown tennis ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

baseball.note: Nearly perfect, but the hit should sound like a wooden bat.
baseball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown baseball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

softball.note: Like the baseball: the hit should sound like a real bat.
softball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown softball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

beach-ball.plan: A real plastic beach-ball bounce each time it lands (no boing), and a light slap as it's punched up.

golf-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown golf ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

bowling-ball.note: Close, but too toy-like: it should sound like a ball rolling down a real lane and real pins falling.
bowling-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown bowling ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

pool-ball.note: Too high-pitched and hollow; it should sound solid, like a real cue striking a pool ball.
pool-ball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown pool ball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

pickleball.note: The whistling is annoying; change it unless it's truly realistic.
pickleball.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown pickleball lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft.

marble.note: Same sound, quieter by default (or a slightly better real marble recording).
marble.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a thrown marble lands with its own sound, from its tap's own cues (louder the harder it lands). On the board: three landings, hard to soft. The tap keeps the same real marble roll, about 6 dB quieter (Sound C).

solar-system.note: Pretty cool, but a little less robotic or electronic would be better; it's fine to keep if needed.
solar-system.plan: No synth chord: a soft whoosh as the planets swing into line, a warm flare as the corona shows, and a whoosh as they swing on.

mercury.note: It doesn't match the effect (a fast spin while the sunlit side glows red hot and shimmers).
mercury.plan: A quick spin whoosh, then a low roar of heat and a soft searing sizzle while the day side glows, fading as it cools (no tone).

earth.plan: The same ocean wash (a little softer) and chime, with the wind turned right down (softer, shorter and quieter).

mars.note: The wind is a little weird; okay, but could be a bit better.
mars.plan: The dust storm is quieter and darker: a softer hiss of dust and a lower wind.

saturn.note: He doesn't like the robotic noise.
saturn.plan: Two soft icy sweeps as the waves ripple out across the rings, with a faint glitter (no synth shimmer).

uranus.note: Drop the bell-like tone at the start; add a small sound while it rolls (not loud wind).
uranus.plan: A soft low rumble as it rolls to the right, and again as it rolls back (no bell).

aurora-planet.plan: Now: The same aurora air, much lower and gentler (Sound C).

asteroid.note: It doesn't sound like it's breaking apart.
asteroid.plan: A rock crack and a muffled boom, real rocks crumbling apart, a soft grinding as the rubble comes back, and the stone settling.

comet.note: It sounds like wind or a waterfall; it should sound more like something on fire.
comet.plan: A real burning torch roaring as the jets and tails flare, fading as they die back.

meteor.note: It should audibly explode at the end: reuse the star's burst sound, in sync.
meteor.plan: Now: The streak's fire, then the star's own burst (over a short crack) as it explodes at 0.37 s, in time with the fireball (Sound C).

star.note: Drop the robotic song; realistic sounds of it bursting like an explosion, without overwhelming wind.
star.plan: A deep stellar roar as it swells, low throbs as the red giant pulses, a real explosion as it puffs off its shell, and a soft roar as a new star lights.

pulsar.note: The "vroom" buzz and the clicking are annoying; it should sound more epic.
pulsar.plan: A deep boom and rumble as it spins up, and a deep pulse with each flash instead of a tick.

black-hole.note: The low buzz as the star spirals in should be more dramatic and less robotic.
black-hole.plan: A deep growing roar as the star spirals in, a rushing whoosh, a huge low boom as it plunges, and the gas swirling down after it.

star-cluster.plan: Now: Two faint, soft swells of air; much quieter, no hiss (Sound C).

planetary-nebula.note: The robotic music is weird; change it completely.
planetary-nebula.plan: A small burst as the star flares, a whoosh as the shock ring expands, and a deep soft boom as it pushes the main ring out.

nebula.note: Like the star cluster, he doesn't like the little chimes; change it a little.
nebula.plan: A soft fiery flare for each of the seven new stars as it lights (no chimes).

supernova.note: It sounds like the ocean or wind, not an explosion.
supernova.plan: A real deep explosion with a long rumble, over the fiery roar.

virus.note: Drop the little sound at the end of the animation.
virus.plan: The same ripple, squish and pops as the copies bud, without the shimmer at the end.

red-blood-cell.note: It sounds like a little whistle; a little weird.
red-blood-cell.plan: A soft, gel-like squish as it stretches into a crescent, and a soft wobble as it relaxes (no squeaks).

neuron.note: It's just a lot of clicking; it should sound more like electricity.
neuron.plan: A real crackling electric arc running down the axon, and a brighter burst at the terminals.

astrocyte.note: Almost perfect; only the first sound should be less robotic or a different tune.
astrocyte.plan: A soft airy swell as the calcium wave spreads (no synth shimmer), then the same soft wash as the vessel widens.

dna.note: The zip isn't quite in sync with the unzipping; sync it or find a better zipper recording (flexible).
dna.plan: Now: The real zipper timed to the strands: a quick zip as they fly open, a slower one as they close up (3.45 s) (Sound C).

white-blood-cell.note: Mostly good, with a bit less clicking.
white-blood-cell.plan: A soft squishy membrane reaching out (no flutter clicks), the same gulp as it swallows, and a quieter fizz as it digests.

chromosome.note: Realistic sound effects, not a plucked string.
chromosome.plan: A soft sticky tear as the chromatids pull apart, and a soft squish as they come back together (no string, no clacks).

mitochondrion.note: No motor, vroom or buzz. A 'powerhouse' sound such as a furnace; try a few and pick.
mitochondrion.plan: Now: A real gas furnace lighting with a soft whoomp and a warm roar as it powers up, with the ATP sparks' soft pops; no motor, vroom or buzz (candidate A; B is a gas burner's steadier roar) (Sound C).

paramecium.note: Replace the opening shuffle with soft swimming strokes, not wind.
paramecium.plan: Now: A hand moving gently through water: soft strokes through its loop, no shuffle or wind (Sound C).

orbital.note: It's just a little chirp; it should sound a bit more electrical and intricate as the photon is absorbed and sent out.
orbital.plan: A short electric crackle and a rising swish as the photon is absorbed, and a brighter crackle and falling swish as it is given out.

atom.note: No motor sound. Use the periodic table's atom-appear sound (a subtle electric one).
atom.plan: Now: The periodic table's atom sound: a soft electric blip as the electrons speed up and a ping as they blur into rings; no motor (Sound C).

molecule.note: No wind; replace the building-block clicks with something better.
molecule.plan: Now: Soft little ticks of the atoms jostling as it heats, thinning out as it settles; no wind, no building blocks (Sound C).

protein.note: It sounds like wind and building blocks; it should sound like parts separating, then fitting back together.
protein.plan: A real tearing apart as it separates, with a whoosh, then a pressing-together and a soft thud as it reassembles (no building blocks).

crystal-lattice.note: The metal-chain sound is OK; could be better (low priority).
crystal-lattice.plan: Now: One cleaner, softer metallic chime with a faint glassy ring, no rattle after (Sound C).

ruby.note: It needs a different sound: ideally what a real ruby sounds like when tapped.
ruby.plan: A lower real glassy tap and a warm low glow as it lights red.

diamond.note: Find something better: ideally what a real diamond sounds like when tapped.
diamond.plan: A real bright glassy tap, and smaller tinks as the facets flash.

emerald.plan: Now: The crisp gem tap alone, without the whoosh (Sound C).

sapphire.note: Remove the wind and sand-shuffle sound.
sapphire.plan: Now: The crisp gem tap alone, without the wind and sandy shuffle (Sound C).

opal.note: It definitely needs work: it sounds robotic.
opal.plan: A softer, duller real tap and the stone rocking gently on the table (no synth shimmer).

crystal-ball.note: It sounds too robotic; change it.
crystal-ball.plan: A soft misty whoosh and a real crystal glass ringing as the sign rises (no theremin).

heart.plan: Now: The same real heartbeats at the same tempo, about 60 percent louder (Sound C).

brain.note: Replace the wind with a subtle electrical current (related to the neuron's, not the same).
brain.plan: Now: A subtle electric crackle as the sparks race round (softer and lower than the neuron's), and a small snap as the side lights up; no wind (Sound C).

eye.note: The blink sounds like sand or wind; it should be closer to a click.
eye.plan: A soft, small click as the lids close, and a fainter one as they open.

lungs.note: Acceptable; try other inhale and exhale recordings to compare.
lungs.plan: Done (October 7, 2026): the owner picked B, a deep breath, in and out at the same strength; it is now the site sound.

tooth.note: Almost perfect; remove the whistle-like noise at the start.
tooth.plan: A soft polishing swish instead of the squeak, then the same short gleam and sparkles.

oak.note: Close, but the falling leaves don't sound like leaves.
oak.plan: Now: a leafy rustle as the crown rocks, then soft rustles as the loose leaves land (synthesized; no flutter or patter); real CC0 recordings now (oak-leaves.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

pine.note: Drop the chime; if anything, a little Christmas-themed sound.
pine.plan: Now: the needles rustle as it rocks, with a soft jingle of sleigh bells; the snow's hiss and thump stay (no chime).

cherry-blossom.note: A little calm, peaceful, respectful music, and much less wave or wind sound.
cherry-blossom.plan: Now: the opening of the traditional "Sakura Sakura" on a plucked koto-like string, over a faint rustle of petals (no wind).

maple.note: Dial back the wind a little and remove the clicking.
maple.plan: Now: a soft gust and the leaves rustling as they swirl and land (no crunching clicks, much less wind).

bonsai.note: The branch should sound like it's growing and the scissors like real cutting, not a rubber-band bounce and a click.
bonsai.plan: Now: the branch creaks and its leaves rustle as it grows, the scissors open and snip, and the cut piece drops onto the moss; real CC0 recordings now (bonsai-snip.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

willow.note: Basically fine; the wind could be a little less overwhelming.
willow.plan: Now: the same breath of wind, quieter, with the strands rustling.

sunflower.note: Pretty much perfect, but the bouncing noise when the sun appears should change.
sunflower.plan: Now: a warm low swell as the sun comes out (no bouncing tone) and the petals rustling open.

daisy.note: Sync the petal-landing sounds a little better with the falling petals.
daisy.plan: Now: Each petal's soft tap now lands with it: scheduled for the landing itself, so it stays in sync at any frame rate (Sound C).

fern.note: It sounds like shuffling sand or wind, which is awkward.
fern.plan: Now: a soft leafy rustle and a gentle stem creak as each frond unrolls, and again as they roll back up (no sandy flutter).

rocks.note: At the start they sound like building blocks, not stones; the stacking at the end is okay.
rocks.plan: Now: real stone-on-stone knocks as the pile shifts and tumbles home; the stacking knocks stay; real CC0 recordings now (rocks-pebbles.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

campfire.note: Okay, but it clicks too much: remove the clicking and give the flames more sound (the volcano's flame sound would suit).
campfire.plan: Now: the volcano's kind of fire, a low flickering rush with a few soft pops of wood (no clicks).

lava-lamp.note: Drop the acceleration sound; keep the bubbles.
lava-lamp.plan: Now: only the gloops and bubbles (the rising hum is gone).

snow-globe.note: Drop the clicking; the twinkling is okay.
snow-globe.plan: Now: the water sloshing as it is shaken, then the twinkle (no rattle of clicks).

volcano.note: Basically perfect; its flame sound would suit the campfire too.
volcano.plan: Keep the current sound; lend its flame sound to the campfire.

ice-statue.note: Basically perfect; remove the wind-like sound at the start.
ice-statue.plan: Now: the drips and the refreezing; the wind at the start is gone.

iceberg.note: Too much clicking; use a real ice-breaking sound for the ice breaking off.
iceberg.plan: Now: real ice breaking, a deep crack with its groan and splinters (no crackle of clicks), then the splash; real CC0 recordings now (iceberg-crack.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

ice-cream.note: A bit windy, but acceptable as it is (leave it).
ice-cream.plan: Kept as it is (he said it can stay).

watermelon.note: Remove the whoosh at the very start; everything else is fine.
watermelon.plan: Now: no whoosh at the start, only a soft settle; the chops and the fan are unchanged.

birthday-cake.note: It should play part of "Happy Birthday" (the first or last line), like the real song, not a robotic jingle, and no voices.
birthday-cake.plan: Now: blown out with a breath, then the last line of "Happy Birthday to You" on the piano with its chords (no voices); relighting keeps the match; since October 2 (Sound C), on the concert grand's recorded piano notes, at the same tempo.

popcorn.note: It sounds like a sizzle, not real popcorn.
popcorn.plan: Now: a clean, single dry pop for each kernel (ten different real pops, the pot's rumble and the oil's hiss cut out), so each kernel is heard on its own (Sound D).

jelly.plan: Now: a wet, heavy wobble instead of a cartoon boing.

pancakes.note: Remove the click on the flip and it's fine.
pancakes.plan: Now: a smooth sizzle in the pan, the flip and the soft slap as it lands (no crackling ticks).

lollipop.note: Drop the "vroom" noise; keep the wind.
lollipop.plan: Now: only the wind as it spins (the rising "vroom" hum is gone).

candy-cane.note: Remove the little whistle at the start; everything else is fine.
candy-cane.plan: Now: the sugar strains as it twists (no whistle); the snaps and the mends stay.

gummy-bear.note: Remove the whistle at the start; the bounce is fine.
gummy-bear.plan: Now: only the bounce (the whistle is gone).

pretzel.note: Almost perfect; a little more like stretching dough, but fine if it stays.
pretzel.plan: Now: soft dough squished and pulled, with a wet stretching sound.

croissant.plan: Now: the flaky layers shattering softly under the knife, and a smooth butter sizzle (no clicks).

pizza.plan: Now: The bite and a softer, shorter cheese stretch; not windy (Sound C).

burger.plan: Now: the patty's smooth sizzle, no clicking.

taco.note: It sounds like a zipper; it should sound like a hard shell cracking open (the filling dropping out is okay).
taco.plan: Now: a hard shell cracking open; the filling dropping out is unchanged; real CC0 recordings now (taco-crack.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

apple.note: Almost perfect, but the bite sounds like a zipper; it should be a real apple bite.
apple.plan: Now: a crisp bite into an apple (a crunch of tiny fractures and a juicy snap), not a zipper; real CC0 recordings now (apple-bite.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

banana.note: The peel is too loud and sounds like a zipper; make it subtle like a real peel.
banana.plan: Now: A soft rustle as the bunch comes apart, and a quiet real banana peel as each one peels (no zipper) (Sound C).

cherries.note: One of his favorites and basically perfect; just remove the string-like note at the start and keep the bubbly knocking.
cherries.plan: Now: no string note, only the stems' soft swish; the knocking is unchanged.

bricks.note: Pretty much perfect, just a little too high-pitched.
bricks.plan: Now: a lower plastic clack, for the tap and each brick landing.

spinning-top.note: The spin sound more subtle, in sync with the speed (louder as it spins faster), including when you spin it yourself.
spinning-top.plan: Now: A soft flick as it starts; its spin is a quiet real hum that follows its speed (louder and a little higher when fast, gone as it slows), also when a drag spins it (Sound C).

dice.note: It's a plinking, twinkling sound; it should sound like real dice thrown on a table.
dice.plan: Now: two dice thrown on a wooden table, bouncing with quicker, quieter knocks and settling; real CC0 recordings now (dice-throw.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback. In Hands-on (lane Hands-on H1), each die clacks as it lands, a brighter clack when two dice knock (the candidate below).

newtons-cradle.note: Almost perfect and close to the real thing; keep it (a slightly more metallic version is only worth a try).
newtons-cradle.plan: Keep the current sound; at most, offer one slightly more metallic candidate to compare, with the current one as the default.

teddy-bear.note: Sounds like wood stretching; make it a subtle soft, plush sound.
teddy-bear.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a soft, plush thud as it lands. The tap keeps the soft rustle of a plush bear's fabric and stuffing; no creak (Sound C).

yo-yo.note: It sounds like wind; it should sound like a real yo-yo.
yo-yo.plan: Now: the string unwinding, the whirr at the bottom and the smack back into the hand.

puzzle-cube.note: He likes it, but it should sound less like a toy and more like a real puzzle cube turning, almost ASMR-like.
puzzle-cube.plan: Now: each turn a plastic slide over the ridges and a soft clack as the layer seats; real CC0 recordings now (puzzle-cube-turn.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

spring-toy.note: Not good: make it sound like a real Slinky (a shimmering, almost sandy metallic sound).
spring-toy.plan: Now: A real metal Slinky's shimmering coils as it walks (Sound C).

kite.note: Okay, but the wind is too strong; dial it back.
kite.plan: Now: the same, with the wind dialed back.

paper-plane.note: The wind a little too loud.
paper-plane.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a light paper slap as it lands. The tap keeps the same fold and glide, with the air lower (Sound C).

origami-crane.plan: Now: in Hands-on, a soft paper flutter as the tail hits its stops.

balloon-dog.note: Remove the whistle at the start, and the pop should be a real balloon pop.
balloon-dog.plan: Now: a real balloon bursting (no whistle first); real CC0 recordings now (balloon-dog-pop.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback. In Hands-on (lane Hands-on H1), a long rubbery squeak when squeezed, a short one as it lands (the candidate below).

soap-bubbles.note: Blowing wind softer; the bubbles a little louder and more like real bubbles.
soap-bubbles.plan: Now: A soft breath through the wand, and a soft real pop as each bubble bursts while it's blown (Sound C).

robot.note: Awkward; it should sound like a real wind-up toy.
robot.plan: Now: a few clicks of the winding key, then clockwork whirring as it unwinds and its tin feet clanking along; real CC0 recordings now (robot-wind.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback. In Hands-on (lane Hands-on H1), the key clicks as it is wound and ticks as it unwinds (the candidate below).

chess-set.note: Okay, but not a good chess sound; use better chess-piece sounds, like the good online-chess themes.
chess-set.plan: Now: pieces set down on a felted wooden board, a woody thock (a sharper one for captures), like a good online-chess theme; real CC0 recordings now (chess-set-move.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

book.note: We should hear the pages flip like a real book's, not wind.
book.plan: Now: real paper pages turning (no wind); real CC0 recordings now (book-page.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

laptop.note: Basically perfect: keep the clicks and the screen-on sound, but remove the thunk when it closes and the twinkle when it opens, and make the keys sound more realistic.
laptop.plan: Now: opening keeps only the screen-on sound (no twinkle), closing has no thunk, and the keys sound like a real keyboard (a tick and a thock).

clock.note: Like the other alarm clock, it should sound more realistic.
clock.plan: Now: a real wind-up alarm clock, the hammer rattling between its two bells, in two rings.

desk-fan.note: Too much like a "vroom"; it should sound more like real fan blades spinning up or down, not windy.
desk-fan.plan: Now: the blades' soft thrum of air swelling in as it starts and fading as it stops (no rising motor hum).

shield.note: Remove the clicking as the shield moves (he dislikes clicking on almost every toy).
shield.plan: Now: the clang and the gleam's shimmer, no crackling clicks.

bow-and-target.note: Pretty good, but the string sounds like a guitar.
bow-and-target.plan: Now: a real bowstring's thump and the arrow's hiss, not a guitar-like note; the hit is unchanged; real CC0 recordings now (bow-and-target-release.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

trebuchet.note: Pretty good, but the wind is too dramatic, and he'd like to hear the wood straining.
trebuchet.plan: Now: the timber beam creaks and strains, then a softer swing (much less wind).

crossbow.note: Remove the click and change the instrument-like bow sound; the hit on the target is fine.
crossbow.plan: Now: no click; the string's real thump, then the bolt hitting as before; real CC0 recordings now (bow-and-target-release.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

knights-helmet.note: All right, if basic; okay for now.
knights-helmet.plan: Keep the current sound for now.

crown.note: Very close, but the trumpet is too robotic; it should be a real royal trumpet.
crown.plan: Now: the fanfare on a natural trumpet (a lip scoop, breath and late vibrato) instead of synthetic brass; the jewels' pings stay.

wizards-orb.note: The wind is odd and the twinkling cliché; find something else.
wizards-orb.plan: Now: a deep, slow hum of power swelling in the glass (no wind or twinkles).

jellyfish.plan: Now: The same two swimming pulses, a little louder (Sound C).

ladybug.plan: Now: The same wing whirr, about 5 dB quieter (Sound C).

snail.note: It could sound a little wetter, like slime.
snail.plan: Now: wetter and slimier, a squish with a sticky stretch.

octopus.note: The ink sounds like wind; it should sound like bubbling liquid.
octopus.plan: Now: a squirt, then the ink bubbling out as a liquid (no wind).

starfish.note: Keep the current sound, and add a small sound synced to the arms as they open and close (nice, not necessary).
starfish.plan: Now: the pop is kept, and each arm makes a soft wet lift as it rises and a soft pat as it settles, one after another.

frog.note: Okay but cartoonish: a more realistic fly buzz, and a real croak or ribbit after it eats the fly.
frog.plan: Now: a real fly's wandering buzz, and real croaks after it eats the fly; real CC0 recordings now (frog-fly.mp3, frog-croak.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

owl.note: The hoot is too long and sounds like a dog howling: a short, natural owl hoot recording.
owl.plan: Now: A short, natural owl hoot (h'HOO-oo and a soft hoo), about 1 s (Sound C).

lorenz.note: One of his least favorite sounds (a weird whistling howl); it should sound more epic.
lorenz.plan: Now: something epic, a deep hit, a dark slow rush and a wide low chord (no whistling howl).

hypercube.note: One of his favorite toys but least favorite sounds: the "vroom" acceleration; use something else.
hypercube.plan: Now: no "vroom"; a great slow rush as it turns inside out and again as it turns home, over a low chord.

torus-knot.note: He doesn't like the banjo or guitar notes; it should be sound effects instead.
torus-knot.plan: Now: it strains as it is pulled and lets go with a real thump and swish (no banjo or guitar notes).

gyroid.note: The accelerating noise and bubbles are awkward; change it.
gyroid.plan: Now: slow rushes one way and back over a low chord (no rising hum, no bubbles).

mandelbulb.plan: Keep the current sound; use it as the model for the Mandeltorus.

surface-plotter.note: Both the ocean-like wave and the "vroom" are overwhelming; it needs something subtle.
surface-plotter.plan: Now: subtle, a soft low chord swelling as the surface rises (no wave, no "vroom").

unit-circle.note: Okay, but a little too robotic; explore some options.
unit-circle.plan: Now: warmer, a soft low chord that swells with the turn and a gentle rush a quarter turn later (one option to try).

fourier-circles.note: He likes it, even if it's a little robotic.

neural-network.note: One of his favorite toys, but it sounds like a child's xylophone; make it cooler, more exciting or intense.
neural-network.plan: Now: more intense, an electric surge as each layer lights over a dark chord, a deep hit at the answer and crackling current as the pulses run back.

cnn.note: The sounds are fine, and he likes that they match across the poster, the 3D model and the draw-a-digit view.
cnn.plan: Keep the current sounds, the same across all three views.

rnn.note: Fine, but change the "vroom" acceleration sound.
rnn.plan: Now: a soft pulse of current as each word goes in and the loop's chord growing a note each time (no rising hum).

transformer.note: Not terrible; of its four sounds, the first two are robotic and should change.
transformer.plan: Now: the first two sounds are warm swells of current instead of electronic shimmers; the last two are unchanged.

diffusion-model.note: Not bad and could be a little better: the closing chord is a little robotic.
diffusion-model.plan: Now: a soft dark swell as the noise clears (no sandy hiss) and a chord rolled on the piano as the duck appears.

gradient-descent.plan: Now: a soft tap as the ball lands each of its 21 hops down, in sync, and one as it lands home (the falling tone and whoosh are gone).

half-adder.note: Pretty much fine; remove the fly-like buzz near the end.
half-adder.plan: Now: the buzz near the end is gone; the rest is unchanged.

decorated-tree.note: Jingle Bells on a nicer instrument (real chimes or bells, or a better piano).

menorah.plan: Now: a match struck, then each wick catching with a soft flame as it lights, one by one; going out, a small puff as each flame goes out in turn (no big gust).

rocket.note: It could be a little more realistic.
rocket.plan: Now: the flickering roar of the exhaust over a deep rumble.

helicopter.note: It should sound like real rotor blades chopping.

gaussian-splatting.note: Training view: drop the opening chord; instead of the xylophone notes, a subtle, continuous descending tone as the loss curve is drawn. gaussian-splatting.plan: Now: Training, a soft tone falling as the loss curve draws (no chord or notes); one splat, a soft airy swell; many splats, a fainter twinkle; sorting, a pebble's click for each splat as it is placed, in sync, each a little different (Sound C).

photo-album.note: Thud is fine, but page turn swish doesn't sound realistic.
photo-album.plan: Now: a thick card page turning and the thud; real CC0 recordings now (book-page.mp3), with the synthesized sound as a fallback.

photo-3d.note: Doesn't need to sound like wind. No whoosh necessary.
photo-3d.plan: Now: a Sound choice in the Toy tab (lane Photo depth): Paper (as it is), a soft chime, pop-up layers (four plucks as the layers rise, and down as they settle), a water drop, none, or your own sound (kept on the device). On the board: the three new ones, rising then settling 3 s later.

fluid-lab.plan: Pours, glugs and splashes in sync with the animation, from real recordings (lane Fluids, r4). Honey a little louder: done by lane Sound C (its gloops about 3 dB up, src/fluids/runtime.js).

periodic-table.note: The whoosh on tapping an element: keep it but much more subtle. Add a faint sound in sync with each proton and neutron packing into the nucleus (not bubbles, not plastic blocks). Then (October 6): the ticks grate like nails on a chalkboard; make them more like the splat simulator's sorting.
periodic-table.plan: Now: in the site and new to hear (lane Elements, October 6, 2026): for each proton and neutron as it packs into the nucleus, a soft pebble's click like the splat simulator's sorting, instead of the bright 2.7 to 3.3 kHz clacks (Sound C). On the board, iron's nucleus (26 protons, 30 neutrons): A, the new clicks; B, the old clacks to compare.

shardball.note: A new sound for a brick breaking.
shardball.plan: Now in the game (lane Arcade r2): a glazed brick breaks with a wooden marimba note, one note of a pentatonic scale per row (higher rows ring higher, so clearing a column climbs), and a short dry crumble as it falls apart; a stone brick with a low knock and a longer, gritty crumble. No glass ring. The ball's knocks off the paddle and the walls stay as they were.

page-breaker.note: A new sound for a word's block breaking; the game's other sounds stay.
page-breaker.plan: Now in the game (lane Arcade r2): a word's block tears off the page with a real paper flap (a recording, a touch higher or lower block by block) over a light crumple. The paddle's and the walls' knocks stay as they were.

stollen.note: No zipper-like clicking; the note is too loud.
stollen.plan: Now: just the two soft plucked notes, much quieter; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

orange-photo.note: One bubble, not two, and subtler.
orange-photo.plan: Now: one soft pop, quieter; the second bubble (the drips) is gone (Sound D).

physalis.note: No zipper-like clicking and no twinkles.
physalis.plan: Now: the berry's soft papery pop in its husk and a light landing; no clicking rustle, no twinkle (Sound D).

crystal-gem.plan: Now: one quiet glassy ring, shorter; the sparkle is gone (Sound D).

monkey-doll.note: Keep the rubber-band sound; remove the clicking after it.
monkey-doll.plan: Now: the rubber-band boing only; the clicking rustle after it is gone (Sound D).

sunflower-photo.note: A new, subtle sound: no clicking, stretching or wind.
sunflower-photo.plan: Now: a soft, warm low chord as the flower lifts and a light landing; no clicking, flutter or wind (Sound D).

white-roses.note: Remove the clicking; keep the glass ding.
white-roses.plan: Now: the vase's glass ding only; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

bonsai-photo.plan: Now: the pot's wooden knock only; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

mushroom-photo.plan: Now: the soft pop only; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

crochet-earth.plan: Now: the soft boing only; the twinkle is gone (Sound D).

maple-tree.note: Remove the clicking; the wind is all right but subtler.
maple-tree.plan: Now: a gentle gust of wind, about half as loud; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

peony.plan: Now: the vase's glass note only; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

money-tree.plan: Now: the pot's soft knock only; the clicking rustle is gone (Sound D).

point-clouds.note: The wind is too loud; make it subtler, and the twinkle a little subtler too.
point-clouds.plan: Now: the same lidar sweep with the airy wind at half its level and the twinkle a little quieter (Sound D).

unit-cells.note: A new toy's sound, for the owner to hear.
unit-cells.plan: New (lane Lattices and orbitals): a small, clear glass clink as the view steps, and a soft wooden tick as the atoms settle.

orbital-atlas.note: A new toy's sound, for the owner to hear.
orbital-atlas.plan: New (lane Lattices and orbitals): a soft, low whoosh as the orbital is cut open, and a quiet low ding as its cut face shows.

solar-orbits.note: A new labs toy: the solar system on real orbits.
solar-orbits.plan: Space is silent: a soft, low breath as the view flies to the next planet, like the other real-space toys.

sushi-boat.note: Keep the first sound; remove the second little beat.
sushi-boat.plan: Now: the wooden knock only, as the boat rocks; the little second beat is gone (Photoreal r3).

seeded-loaf.note: It sounds like a zipper: something very subtle instead.
seeded-loaf.plan: Now: one very soft thud as the loaf lands; no crunch (Photoreal r3).

steak.note: Not the right sound; something fitting and not overwhelming.
steak.plan: Now: a quiet, soft slap as the steak lands on each side (it flips over and back); no hiss (Photoreal r3).

alum-crystal.plan: Now: no ding: a soft stony knock as the crystal is set back on its block (Photoreal r3).

puffin.plan: Now: soft landings as it hops (no flutter); a real puffin's call, from a CC0 or CC BY recording, is still to come (Photoreal r3).

toy-trex.note: They sound like wind: a subtle bounce sound instead.
toy-trex.plan: Now: a subtle plastic tap as the toy rocks on its feet; no roar or wind (Photoreal r3).

elephant-souvenir.note: They sound like wind: a subtle bounce sound instead.
elephant-souvenir.plan: Now: two soft, heavy steps as it turns; no wind (Photoreal r3).

cave-lioness.note: Wind and far too loud: replace it.
cave-lioness.plan: Now: one quiet, low, soft breath out as she looks round; no wind or roar (Photoreal r3).

dog-plush.note: Sounds like a rubber band: replace it.
dog-plush.plan: Now: the soft thump of a plush landing, twice; no boing (Photoreal r3).

bmx-bike.note: Remove the bell; a softer opening sound.
bmx-bike.plan: Now: a soft, dull knock as it leans on its kickstand, and a lighter one as it rocks back; no bell (Photoreal r3).

murex-shell.note: Remove the clicking; keep the ding, more subtle.
murex-shell.plan: Now: the ding only, quieter and shorter; no clicking (Photoreal r3).

cactus-real.note: No clicking; softer notes, like the first cactus.
cactus-real.plan: Now: one soft plucked note, like the first cactus's; no clicking (Photoreal r3; a single note, as the sound lint keeps tunes to the music shelf).

desk-globe.note: Spin it, with no wind or suction sound.
desk-globe.plan: Now: the globe spins in its stand, with one soft, hollow knock as it is flicked round; no wind or suction (Photoreal r3).

cherry-blossom-photo.note: The bounce is fine; no twinkle.
cherry-blossom-photo.plan: Now: the bounce's soft flutter only; no twinkle (Photoreal r3).

triceratops-skull.plan: Now: A low, soft knock of bone as the skull turns to look.

cone-shell.plan: Now: A soft porcelain tick as the shell turns.

celestial-globe.plan: Now: A gentle wooden creak as the globe is set turning.

armillary-sphere.plan: Now: A quiet brass ring as the inner rings turn.

stannern-meteorites.plan: Now: Five soft stony thuds as the stones land, one after another.

fluorite-crystal.plan: Now: A low, soft hum while the lamp is on.

ammonite-agate.plan: Now: A stone-on-wood knock as the fossil is laid on its other face.

morasko-meteorite.plan: Now: A deep, quiet ring of iron.

megalodon-tooth.plan: Now: A dull stone tap as the tooth is laid on its other side.

volume-viewer.note: No click and no rising hum.
volume-viewer.plan: Now in the site (lane Fix10): a tap slides a film onto a lightbox (a papery slip and a soft settle); Play has its own dark, soft rush for each pass of the cut; the drag is silent. On the board: the tap, then Play's two rushes.

photo-dash.note: A better sound for catching a spark (the coin).
photo-dash.plan: Now in the game (lane Arcade r3): two quick bright bell notes up a fourth (B5, then E6) with a faint glint, in place of the old scattered sparkle. Each ball also lands with its own sound: the glass marble clinks, the steel ball rings, the beach ball thumps hollow, and the tennis ball pocks.

note-rider.note: Each note should stop at its own length; add guitar and other instruments to choose from.
note-rider.plan: Now in the game (lane Arcade r3): a caught note lasts its own length. On the keyboards the key lifts and the damper falls when the note ends; a plucked string fades over about the note's length. Seven instruments to pick from a row of buttons in the game (and the Instrument option): piano, guitar, steel guitar, harp, organ, synth, and vibes. A recording still plays its own slices. Each candidate below is the start of Ode to Joy as the game plays it.

qr-anatomy.note: The wind under the tap, quieter.
qr-anatomy.plan: Now in the site (lane QR r5): the soft breath under the tap at about a third of its old level (0.07 to 0.025); the light wooden knock as a part lifts is a little louder (0.16 to 0.26), so the tap is still heard.

qr-three.note: The whoosh as the codes come apart, quieter.
qr-three.plan: Now in the site (lane QR r5): the whoosh as the three codes slide apart at a third of its old level (0.12 to 0.04); the soft knock as they come back together stays.

barcodes.plan: Now in the site (lane QR r5): only the soft breath as the scanner's line sweeps, a little fuller (0.025 to 0.06) so the tap is still heard; the note of a read at the end is gone.
